correctness.rationale: Definitions and quantifiers reconstructed. An exact 2^n rooted-word exhaustion for each 1<=n<=11 tests all rotations and prefix/factor comparisons, while a proved cyclic-positive-gap composition bijection and independent span criterion rederive the identical three 11-bit obstructions. The 33 exceptional rotations have explicit factor certificates. For every n>=11 the fixed five positions of ones in 00010101011 followed by n-11 zeros leave only five possible one-starting cuts, each disproved at length 2, 3, or 5. Finite tests through length120 are nonessential and do not certify infinity.

value.rationale: The natural normalization question is whether a circular binary sequence can be made ones-prefix normal by choosing its origin, without changing the underlying circular object. The theorem locates the first impossible length sharply, exhaustively classifies all first obstruction necklaces, and gives a transparent persistent obstruction at every longer length. This defines the precise boundary of cyclic rephasing as a normal-form operation; it is neither a trivial short-factor check nor an unmotivated slice. No larger-length full census is claimed.
